lead.headline: Inflation accelerates to 3.7% as gasoline jumps 9.1% in a month
lead.dek: Core prices climb to 2.6%; markets put odds of an Oct. 28 Fed hike above 55% and the Nasdaq falls 1.8%
body: U.S. consumer prices rose 3.7% in the 12 months through September, up from 3.4% in each of the two prior months and above the 3.6% economists expected, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Wednesday, with a 9.1% one-month jump in gasoline accounting for more than half of the increase.

Prices rose 0.6% from August, and core inflation, which excludes food and energy, climbed to 2.6% from 2.4%, above the 2.5% economists had forecast. Energy was up 20.4% from a year earlier and airline fares 22.4%, CBS News reported. Regular gasoline averaged $4.33 a gallon Wednesday, up from $2.98 before the Iran war began, according to AAA.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate to 3.75% to 4% in September, its first increase since 2023, and meets next Oct. 27-28. NBC News reported market odds of an October hike rose above 55% after the release; the Nasdaq fell 1.8% and the S&P 500 1.1%. White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett called the last report before the Nov. 3 midterms "a disappointing number."

briefs.headline: DOJ gives California 48 hours to vet ballots for noncitizens
briefs.summary: Acting Deputy AG Trent McCotter asked counties to set aside mail ballots of possible noncitizens on a federal list. The secretary of state said she got no list.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court halts order forcing fast FCC ad-rate ruling
briefs.summary: The per curiam order blocks a 4th Circuit mandate giving the FCC 48 hours to rule on party ad-rate discounts. Sotomayor and Jackson would have denied it.

briefs.headline: Social Security sets 3.6% cost-of-living increase for 2027
briefs.summary: The adjustment adds about $76 a month, or a little more than $900 a year, for the average retired worker starting in January.

briefs.headline: Texas DA says ICE vehicle struck Houston man intentionally
briefs.summary: Harris County DA Sean Teare said video shows an unmarked ICE vehicle swerved into Miguel Parra Hernandez Saturday. ICE called that "RECKLESS and FALSE."

briefs.headline: School roof collapse kills 27 pupils and teacher in Peshawar
briefs.summary: A Lady Reading Hospital official told AFP at least 27 pupils and a teacher died when a private school's roof fell Thursday. More than 30 were hurt.

briefs.headline: Istanbul floods kill teenager, shut schools across city
briefs.summary: Authorities logged 1,277 floods and 15 landslides overnight; the governor's office said a 14-year-old was electrocuted. Classes were off Thursday.

briefs.headline: Kenya confirms second Ebola case in first patient's family
briefs.summary: The ministry said a 39-year-old relative of the man who died Oct. 5 fell ill Tuesday in quarantine. Kenya is the fourth nation with a DRC-linked case.

briefs.headline: Thousands march in Colombia against new president's agenda
briefs.summary: Unions, students and Indigenous groups rallied in Bogota and Medellin Wednesday, the first large protests since Abelardo de la Espriella took office.

briefs.headline: Boone jury hears openings in granddaughter starvation trial
briefs.summary: Prosecutors said Wednesday the 14-year-old died of severe malnutrition in a home with plenty of food; the defense said a tragedy is not a crime.

briefs.headline: State school board calls funding formula unconstitutional
briefs.summary: The board voted Wednesday to argue in the pending Supreme Court case that the formula is inadequate; a department plan puts special education at $190M.

briefs.headline: West Virginia sues OpenAI in Mason County over child safety
briefs.summary: Attorney General McCuskey filed Wednesday in Mason County Circuit Court, alleging ChatGPT lacks age checks and coached users toward self-harm.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court weighs admonishment of Judge Sweeney
briefs.summary: Justices heard arguments Wednesday on a JIC admonishment over the Pleasants County judge's CPS staffing order, interviews and Facebook posts.

regional.item: Huntington council voted 8-1 Tuesday to ban engine compression brakes citywide, with signs to be posted.
Charleston police are adding officers to bus routes after nearly a dozen close calls with drivers passing stopped buses.
Williamstown Elementary sent students home Wednesday after a phoned bomb threat; a search with a dog found no device.

away.item: Pownal named three members Oct. 8 to a study group on a regional EMS district merging the Bennington and Pownal rescue squads.

hotspots.item: The EDA's plan to buy 50-plus DNR acres across from Big Ditch Lake became a possible lease after DNR said a sale needs state approval, the Echo said Wednesday.
Autumn With Topsail runs Friday through Sunday on the Historical Society grounds in Topsail Beach, with more than 110 artists and a Kiwanis pancake breakfast.

briefs.headline: Northern Health leads B.C. in drug-death rate, coroner says
briefs.summary: BC Coroners Service preliminary data put the region at 43 deaths per 100,000 this year. Prince George has 36 so far, after 67 in 2025 and 107 in 2024.

briefs.headline: Police car and truck collide on Highway 16, closing road
briefs.summary: RCMP said a cruiser carrying two people under arrest hit a transport truck at Tabor Lake Road East early Wednesday. Injuries were called non-serious.

briefs.headline: Eby, Doerkson and Lowan clash on deficit, ICBC and DRIPA
briefs.summary: Doerkson said Wednesday he would repeal the Indigenous rights act, Eby asked how $5B in Tory promises is funded and Lowan pitched a $5.4B-a-year wealth tax.

briefs.headline: NDP costing shows B.C. deficit falling to $12B by 2028-29
briefs.summary: The party said Wednesday its promises are covered by taxing the top 3.88% of earners, with $581M to spare. Eby said Tory tax cuts would blow a budget hole.

briefs.headline: Smith votes to stay as 174,532 Albertans cast early ballots
briefs.summary: The premier said in a video Wednesday that "Canada can still work" and urged yes on the other nine questions. Day one of advance polls beat 2023's daily average.

briefs.headline: FSIN sues Ottawa over $12.4M in disputed spending
briefs.summary: The federation of 74 Saskatchewan First Nations rejected Indigenous Services Canada's final ruling that the spending was ineligible. Chief Bobby Cameron said $8M was PPE.

briefs.headline: Satellites catch nearly all methane plumes in blind test
briefs.summary: A Stanford-led Nature study ran 481 controlled releases in Arizona in 2025; dedicated methane satellites detected 92% to 100% of plumes.

briefs.headline: Roman telescope's main instrument beats focus target
briefs.summary: NASA said the Wide Field Instrument's optical error measured 63 nanometers against a 90-nanometer requirement, about 30% better than predicted.

briefs.headline: Warwick team finds green and pink white dwarfs nearby
briefs.summary: Five of 151 white dwarfs within 65 light years would look yellow or pink to the eye, the University of Warwick said, and one is modeled as green.

briefs.headline: Candida auris copies its whole genome to survive drugs
briefs.summary: Exeter-led researchers said in Nature Communications the fungus made extra copies of its genome to survive antifungals; bloodstream cases kill 45%.

briefs.headline: Covert AI bias sways choices of 233 trial participants
briefs.summary: Participants picked the unfavorable option five to eight times more often when an AI adviser covertly pushed it, HKU and Tsinghua said in PNAS.

briefs.headline: UK still weighing AI measures for cyber security bill
briefs.summary: Civil servant Alexandra Jones told MPs the government is "looking at" amendments; committee chair Liam Byrne said a bill must legislate, not consider.

briefs.headline: DeepMind reports no AI-driven speedup in its research
briefs.summary: Google's Gemini 4 safety report says code changes fully delegated to AI rose from 7.5% to 11.9%; capability growth held at 0.1 index points a month.
